name: Squarespace
tagline: Hosted website builder for portfolios, businesses, blogs, and stores

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked; 2026 public coverage lists Basic around $25/month monthly and lower annual pricing.

verdictSummary: A portfolio or marketing site is easy to build, but Squarespace's paid value is templates, editor, hosting, commerce/forms, domains, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Generate a static site from templates, add a small CMS, host it, and configure domain/forms.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because it removes design, hosting, and maintenance from the website project.

priorArt.name: WordPress
priorArt.desc: Open-source CMS/site platform; a practical alternative for many Squarespace use cases.

alternatives.name: Microweber
alternatives.desc: Drag-and-drop pages, blogging and ecommerce without a licence bill; hosting and updates move in with you.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or upload the PHP package to a web host and complete its browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Site content and settings in a supported SQL database; images and other uploads in server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Microweber gives up Squarespace's consistently polished templates, managed infrastructure and one-vendor support.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs compatible PHP extensions, URL rewriting, a database and correct filesystem permissions

alternatives.name: Odoo Community
alternatives.desc: Website, blog, store, CRM and business apps in one enormous suite; elegance was not the design brief.

facts.install: Use Odoo's packaged installer, source install or Docker image, backed by PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Business and website records in PostgreSQL; uploaded attachments in Odoo's filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo Community is an enormous ERP with a less elegant site-design experience and much heavier administration than Squarespace.
facts.setupBlocker: A production deployment needs PostgreSQL, workers/reverse proxy configuration, backups and ongoing administration of a very large suite

alternatives.name: Vvveb
alternatives.desc: A visual CMS with blog, pages, forms and ecommerce in one install; polished enough, obscure enough to need its manual.

facts.install: Download and upload the PHP release, open the site URL, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Content, products, orders and settings in MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL; media and downloadable files on the server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: Vvveb lacks Squarespace's template polish, managed hosting, integrated support and calm one-vendor experience.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable files, mail and payment configuration, plus ongoing server updates

alternatives.name: WooCommerce
alternatives.desc: WordPress pages, blogs, portfolios and a real store; no platform rent, plenty of plugin and server housekeeping.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A page-builder framework, not a hosted website, blog and store product.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Publii
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent for static portfolios and blogs, but no native store or business operations.

rejectedAlternatives.name: WordPress
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The site and blog are free, but a Squarespace-style store requires installing and maintaining another product.

notes: Mainstream and useful; verdict depends on site complexity.
prompt:
Build me a personal website to replace Squarespace: portfolio, blog, and a contact form. Requirements:

- A static site built with Eleventy: home, about, a projects grid, and a blog.
  Content is Markdown files in content/, front matter for title/date/tags.
- One layout system: a base template plus Nunjucks partials for header/footer/cards,
  system font stack, responsive images via @11ty/eleventy-img. No CSS framework.
- Blog gets tag pages and an RSS feed generated at build time.
- Contact form POSTs to a tiny Express handler that emails me via SMTP creds in .env
  and appends each message to data/messages.jsonl. Honeypot field for spam, no captcha.
- npm run build outputs dist/; npm run deploy rsyncs dist/ to my VPS, served by Caddy
  with automatic HTTPS. Put the Caddyfile snippet in the README.
- No accounts, no telemetry, no CMS database. Content lives in git, edits are commits.
- Out of scope: a drag-and-drop editor, ecommerce, and switchable themes. I edit
  Markdown and CSS directly, that is the trade.
- README: DNS records to set, Caddy snippet, SMTP setup for the form handler.
